why: 0:00-0:22 is the presenter talking. At 0:24-0:34 she only holds the perfboard up in her palm to show it, and it already has an earlier resistor on it. Nothing is laid flat or centred on a work surface; that detail is invented.

edits.instruction: Rub flux paste onto the holes where the resistor will go.
edits.say: Open the tin of soldering flux paste, pick up a little on your fingertip, and rub a thin layer over the silver rings of the holes where the resistor leads will go.
placements: soldering flux paste (pale-yellow, from the round tin) → thin layer rubbed with a fingertip over the silver rings near the D1-D5 end of the green board, where the resistor goes
edits.safety: Flux paste irritates skin and eyes: keep it away from your eyes and wash your hands afterwards.

why: 0:36 a red-lidded paste tin is opened, 0:38-0:40 a fingertip goes into the yellow paste, 0:42-0:44 she rubs it onto the board holes; by 0:46-0:48 she has moved on. It is flux paste, not solder, and it is applied by rubbing, not dabbing.

edits.say: Bend both leads of the small blue resistor down at right angles right next to its body. Push the leads through two holes in the same column, three rows apart, about three holes in from the D1-D5 pads, and press the body flat against the board. Flip the board over and bend both leads flat against the back along the rows.
placements: two silver resistor leads → bent 90° down at the body ends before inserting
small blue resistor body → flat on the top face, lying across the board's short width, about three holes in from the D1-D5 pad end
two silver resistor leads → through two holes in the same column three rows apart, then bent flat against the back along the rows

missing_after: Clamp the board in the helping-hands alligator clip with the solder side up (1:30-1:44): she slides the board into the clip and checks that it holds before picking up the iron.
why: 0:54-0:58 she bends the leads with her fingers; 1:00-1:16 she inserts them and presses the body flat near the D1-D5 pads; 1:18-1:28 she bends the leads flat on the back. The joints at 2:54 sit three rows apart, not in adjacent holes. From 1:30 she is clamping the board, which is a separate step.

edits.say: Wipe the hot iron tip on the damp yellow sponge. Hold the tip against both the silver ring and the lead where it comes out of the hole for about three seconds, then feed solder wire into the joint (not onto the tip) until it forms a small shiny mound. Take the solder away, then the iron. Repeat at the second lead.
placements: soldering iron tip → wiped on yellow sponge, then held against the silver ring and the lead at the first hole
solder wire from the blue Plusivo solder tube → fed into the first joint until a small shiny mound forms
same iron and solder → second lead's hole, three rows up in the same column, until a second shiny mound forms
edits.safety: The iron tip is around 350 °C: hold it only by the grip and put it back in its stand. Keep your face out of the flux smoke, and wash your hands after handling solder.

why: 1:46-1:48 the blue object is the Plusivo solder-wire tube, not the iron (the iron at 1:50 is metal with a dark grip). 1:56-1:58 the tip is wiped on the sponge; 2:00-2:22 the first joint is soldered with smoke rising at 2:04; 2:26-2:32 the second; 2:38-2:40 a touch-up. edits.say: Lift each bent lead slightly and snip it with the small black flush cutters right where it leaves its solder mound, without cutting into the mound. Clear the cut scraps away.
placements: small black flush cutters → closed on each lead right at the edge of its solder mound
two clipped lead scraps → removed from the board and work surface

why: 2:44-2:46 she lifts the upper lead and cuts it; 2:48-2:50 she cuts the lower lead that lies flat along the row. The leads lie flat, not sticking up, so 'just above the mounds' is misleading; 2:54-2:56 show the trimmed joints.
